symptom: `lw a2,dirty; ori a2,a2,1; ld a0,mask; and v1,a0,v1; sw a2,dirty; sd v1,mask; lw v1,dirty; and v1,v1,a1; sw v1,dirty` in retail and the same instructions in the candidate, with the mask constant, the `-5` and the 64-bit mask's load in other registers.
cause: the scheduler moves the load and store of one named global past those of another, so the listing keeps neither statement order; the code generator numbers the temporaries in statement order, and that order decides the colours. With the second `p2DirtyFlags` update written last, its `-5` takes an id after the mask's and colours first; written ahead of the mask's update it colours after it, as in retail. `#pragma schedule off` shows the statement order directly.
spelling: `p2DirtyFlags |= 1; p2DirtyFlags &= ~P2_DIRTY_LIGHTING; p2VertexArrayMask &= ~P2_NORMAL_ARRAYS;`.

title: EE GCC orders memory accesses only within one alias set; a field's or read's type decides the schedule.
symptom: a load issued above a store retail keeps it after, or a store ahead of one retail has first, with the registers of the values around it exchanged as a consequence; no statement order moves it.
cause: two accesses are kept in order when they may alias, and the alias set comes from the lvalue's type. Before register allocation only same-type accesses through the same base are ordered; after it the base registers are set more than once, so every pair in one alias set is ordered, and an access of another type (a pointer read among integer stores) is outside that chain, gets low priority and is issued ahead of the first store. Every pointer type is a set of its own, apart from `int` and from the other pointer types: a `void *` store and a function-pointer load are independent.
spelling: the field's real type. Giving a field the same pointer type as another, or reading a reply through its true type, changes the order of the instructions around it; an IOP buffer field typed `void *` instead of `int` gives retail's load and store order.
unit_text: `src/sony/libpad/libpad.c`, `src/cri/sndf.c` (0x281df0), `src/cri/sfadx.c` (0x29c500, matched with the renderer pointer and its neighbours left untyped), `src/cri/cvfs.c`.
notes: Reading it: compile the unit once with `-fno-strict-aliasing`. When the difference shrinks, the cause is a pair of accesses in different sets, and the types of those two lvalues are the ones to settle. The flag is a property of a whole unit, never a fix for one function: on every CRI unit at once it breaks about 50 of them. The CVFS unit keeps its SDK types (function-pointer slots, a `void *` argument block) and its row carries the flag ([CRI CVFS](cri-cvfs.md#argument-block-and-aliasing)).

title: An enum field or parameter has an alias set of its own.
symptom: a load from a header or state struct issued above stores retail keeps it after, or stores out of retail's order, around a few fields that look like plain `int`s.
cause: ee-gcc 2.96 gives an enum type its own alias set, apart from `int`. A store to an enum-typed field, or through an enum-typed pointer parameter, no longer conflicts with the `int` accesses around it, and the scheduler moves them across it. Every field involved has to be an enum (one left `int` leaves 2 to 22 words); one shared enum type works as well as four, `long` does not.
spelling: the SDK's enum types: the coded-picture fields of the MPEG-2 picture attributes (`M2vFrameRate`, `M2vPicType`, `M2vPicStruct`), the luminance key `MwsfdLumiKey *` of the Sofdec effect getter, the user-data level of the MPV handle (`MpvUdLevel`, whose store otherwise holds back the header counter's increment) and the ring id a Sofdec transfer slot reads (`SfdBufId`, whose load retail issues past the out-parameter stores).

title: A read through a union member conflicts with every store.
symptom: a pointer load retail keeps behind stores of every type: `int` out-parameters and pointer out-parameters alike, where a `void *` field is reordered past the `int` stores and an `int` field past the pointer ones, so no single field type fits all its readers.
cause: ee-gcc 2.96 gives any access whose path passes through a union member alias set 0, which conflicts with every other set. A small test file under `-O2 -G0` shows it: a field read twice around an `int *` store is loaded once when the field is an enum, `short` or pointer, and twice when it is `int`, `unsigned`, `long` or a member of a union.
spelling: the field as a union of the types it holds. The work handle of a Sofdec transfer slot is `union { void *obj; SfdMpv *mpv; } hn` (`SfdMpsPrm *prm` in the MPS slot), read as `streams.hn.mpv`. Retail's order then follows in three functions with no other change, and a fourth matches with its natural `SfdSlot **` out-parameters in place of `void **` ones. A *store* through a union conflicts the same way: where retail reloads `*out` before every store of a block, the destination fields sit in a union (the Sofdec frame information keeps its details from offset 72 in a union with the seven words the MWSFD player copies on unchanged), and the block's other loads stay behind each store. The fields before it are enums and pointers (`SfdPicType`, `SfdBufFmt`, `void *buf`, `SfdSjChunk *picUsr`), copied from the MPEG-2 picture attributes whose coded-picture fields are enums too (`M2vPicAtr`, one definition shared with the M2V decoder): a source field read once for a store and a test needs its enum type to differ from the destination's.

title: An address-taken local's alias set depends on what the file compiled before it.
symptom: loads of address-taken locals (a local whose address went to a call, read afterwards) ordered against a store differently from retail with unchanged C, in a function that matches or stops matching when another function is added, removed or moved earlier in the file.
cause: when a scalar local's address is taken, `gen_mem_addressof` turns its register rtx into a memory reference in place and sets only the low word of the alias set; the high word keeps whatever the garbage-collected heap held there. A zero word makes the read conflict with every store, a non-zero one with none. The value is fixed for a given file text, so a build is reproducible, but a change to any function compiled earlier can flip it. Forcing the word non-zero under gdb, with the C unchanged, makes such a function byte-identical to retail.
unit_text: `src/cri/sfmpv.c` (0x2a49b8 matched once the unit's later declarations and functions were in place, with its own C unchanged; 0x2a6f28 flips with the functions before it; 0x2a5c28 flips with the length of an identifier declared earlier in the file, so even a rename can move it: a helper's name of 15 characters or more there reorders its loads, one of 14 or fewer does not; in 0x2a4468 a picture-attribute result is copied to a local, since read from the address-taken slot it reloads after the stores to the handle; 0x2a68e8 matched by declaring its frame pointer and the two error-count locals, in that order, right after the initialised pointers).
notes: Reading it: draft the unit in address order, add each function in its place and re-run the whole unit after each; when a function differs only in such loads, the missing piece is an earlier function, not its own source. A function that matches in a small file can lose it in the full unit, and the reverse.

Where the word comes from: the register rtx is a 32-byte object of the collected heap, and the word is the stale +16 word of that slot's previous occupant. The heap is swept only a few times per unit (twice in `src/cri/sfmpv.c`), and after a sweep a function's declarations are expanded in order into the freed slots: a register and two or three list nodes for a plain local, a dozen or more objects for one with an initialiser. So the declaration order of the function itself moves each address-taken local onto a zero or a non-zero slot, and the main file's path string is part of the history: the same unit compiled as an absolute scratch path and as `src/cri/<file>.c` (what the checker and the link pass) can differ. Search with the file in place, compiled from the repository root; tracing `ggc_alloc` and `gen_mem_addressof` in cc1 under gdb gives each slot's stale word, from which a declaration order can be computed instead of searched.

title: In a run of independent stores, the one that ends a register's life is issued first.
symptom: Before register allocation the scheduler breaks a tie between equally ready instructions in favour of the one that frees registers. Stores of one value through one pointer all become ready together, so the last statement, which holds the last use of the pointer and of the value, comes out first and the others follow in source order; a store that ends only one register's life (the second of two 64-bit fields among 32-bit ones, which has the last use of the 64-bit constant) comes right after it. Retail's `+28, +0, +4, ... +24` is therefore a struct reset written in field order, and a source transcribed in retail's order is rotated once more. MWCC emits stores in source order, so such a transcription matches under MWCC and reads as a function built by the other compiler. The `.sched` dump shows it: every store has the same priority and the one carrying the `REG_DEAD` notes heads the ready list.

title: What the filler takes.
symptom: Read from the compiler (0x4c7690) and checked with the block dump. For a branch whose slot the instruction above cannot fill it tries, in order: the first instruction of the target, moved when the target has one predecessor and copied otherwise (an unconditional jump always may; a conditional branch only when the instruction's destination is in neither the live-in nor the live-out set of the block that ends with the branch); then the first instruction of the fall-through block, on the same liveness test and only when that block has **exactly one** predecessor. Loads, stores and calls are never taken. `v0` is live at the exit of every function that does not return a class, `void` ones included, so it is live from entry to the first call of a `void` function; a parameter still in its argument register is live-in to the entry block, so an instruction that reuses that register is not taken there.

title: Slots left empty across a whole function: the predecessor lists were emptied.
symptom: instructions and registers match, and three branches near the end of the function have a `nop` where the candidate fills the slot with the first instruction of the `if` body (12 bytes short). Nested `if`s and inline helpers change nothing.
cause: the block pass that runs before the filler retargets a conditional branch whose target begins with an unconditional jump, deletes a jump to the next block and merges a block into its only predecessor. After any one of these it sets every block's predecessor list to empty and does not rebuild it. With no predecessors recorded the filler takes nothing from a fall-through block anywhere in the function; copies from targets still happen. The optimizer removes such jumps itself, so one reaches the block pass only when it appears in the code generator: a `return` that is not the function's last statement, or a block whose only statement is a copy the register allocator coalesces away.
spelling: the walk of the free list is a `for` loop that reads the head again in its first clause, `else { for (next = self->freeHead; next < end; next += link * 4) { ... } }`, after `next = self->freeHead` was tested in the `if`. The second read is shared with the first, the copy into `next` is coalesced, and the `else` block is left holding only the jump to the loop's test, which the block pass retargets. With `for (; next < end; ...)` the three slots are filled. A `return;` closing the last `if` body gives retail's bytes too (the jump to the epilogue is deleted) and has no reason.

title: A register whose last use fills a delay slot stays live for the filler until the next barrier.
symptom: A loop's closing branch carries the loop-head compare in its slot and leaves a `move a0,…` behind it, where another spelling of the same statements puts that move in the slot and pads the loop head. The filler asks what is live on a branch's other path before it takes an instruction that sets a register, and at a label with no barrier before it the answer is a scan from the start of the function in which a register dies only at a `REG_DEAD` note (`mark_target_live_regs`). An instruction moved into a slot loses those notes (`emit_delay_sequence`). So when a register's last use is the instruction that fills an earlier branch's slot, the register counts as live at every later label, an instruction that sets it cannot leave a branch's fall-through (MIPS has no annul-if-true slot), and the filler copies from the branch target instead, whatever the branch's predicted direction. Which register that is follows from the locals: in the unit below, three fields of one global read into three locals in field order put the global's address in `a0` and the second field in `v1`, and testing the second field straight from the global swaps the two. The compiler binary keeps its symbols, so gdb breakpoints on `fill_slots_from_thread`, `mostly_true_jump`, `own_thread_p` and `mark_target_live_regs` print each decision and the live set behind it.

title: A call to a function compiled earlier in the same file fills its delay slot differently.
symptom: a call whose delay slot takes another instruction than retail's; the caller matches when the callee's body is not compiled before it.
cause: without exceptions ee-gcc 2.96 marks every function whose body it has compiled as unable to throw (`TREE_NOTHROW`). Every later call to it in the same file gets a `REG_EH_REGION` note, and that note changes which instruction the delay-slot filler picks. A callee defined later, or in another file, is called without the note.
unit_text: `src/cri/sndf.c` and `src/cri/sndfcmd.c` (0x2825e0 calling 0x281ac0 in the other file), `src/cri/m2vhdec.c` (0x286010, whose two callees come first).
notes: Reading it: retail's form without the note means the callee's body was not compiled before the caller; when both are in one unit, that places a file boundary or the function order. A call that needs the note needs the callee defined earlier.

title: `bne` with a `nop` where plain C gives `bnel`: the target starts with a `volatile` access.
symptom: retail `bne; nop` with a load at the branch target; every plain spelling gives `bnel` with that load in the annulled slot.
cause: in `fill_eager_delay_slots`, when filling from the fall-through fails, reorg falls back to an annulled fill from the target, whatever the predicted direction. The slot stays empty only when the target's first instruction cannot move, and `resource_conflicts_p` makes a `volatile` memory reference conflict with everything. The same keyword stops jump2 from cross-jumping two identical stores.
spelling: a `volatile` access, which only the owner approves ([source approvals](source-approvals.md)); six control-flow shapes, seven `do { } while (0)` placements and about 20 load orders do not reproduce it.

title: A jump around a loop's entry is a reload gcse put on the back edge.
symptom: a row loop entered by a jump to its own top over a block of reloads, and a `mult` left in the loop that strength reduction would have removed; `for`, `while` and `do`-`while` spellings of the loop all give the plain entry.
cause: the source computes the row pointer before the loop and again at the top of each row. Partial redundancy elimination in gcse finds the base field and `cols * 2` available on entry and inserts their reload on the back edge; `split_edge` places that new block in front of the loop top, so the entry needs a jump around it. `loop.c` skips a loop whose first scanned insn is not a code label, so the row loop is not optimised and its `mult` stays.
spelling: `s = plane->base + cols * 384;` both before a plain `for` row loop and at the top of its body.

title: A second pointer stepping beside the indexed element pointer is the strength-reduced copy, not a variable.
symptom: a table search `for (i = 0; i < n; i++) { p = &table[i]; if (p->field == 0) break; }` whose first test is made on `p` straight from the table address, then `move v1,s0` after that branch, `addiu v1,v1,size` in the loop and `move s0,v1` before each later test, with the count kept. A source pointer stepped by hand (`q++`, `p = q`) gives the same loop body with the copy before the first branch, in its delay slot.
cause: jump copies the loop's test in front of it, with `i` folded to 0. `loop.c` reduces `p = &table[i]` to a new register and sets it in the pre-header, behind the copied test; the second cse pass turns that into a copy of `p`. A variable initialised before the loop is set ahead of the copied test. *The load's address:* `loop.c` also reduces the address `&p->field` to a register of its own (`lw v0,0(a0)`, the table base kept in a register to initialise it) when `p` has exactly one use in the loop: a giv used once takes no other giv in, and the address giv inherits its benefit. With no use of `p` in the loop (`table[i].field`, but the copied test then reads through the table base) or two (a copy to a second variable that the first cse pass keeps), `p`'s giv takes the address in and the load is `lw v0,4(s0)`. A `volatile` load keeps its address whatever the count: the pass runs with `volatile` operands unrecognised, so the rewritten load is rejected.
notes: Reading it: `-dL` lists each giv with its benefit and prints `giv at N combined with giv at M`; the `Sorted combine statistics` line gives a giv that may not combine a 0.

title: A value set in two blocks is coloured by global allocation, never tied to its input.
symptom: registers only: retail puts an `and`/`addu` result in a fresh register (or one shared with another branch), where the plain spelling reuses the register of the operand that dies there; or two branches end in the same store and retail shares it (one `sw` reached by `b`) where ours repeats it.
cause: local-alloc ties the output of an instruction to a dying input only when the output is a pseudo set and used in one block. A named local assigned in both arms of an `if`, or reused for a later step of the computation up to a store after a branch, is a global pseudo: global-alloc colours it, and when both arms then end in the same register, jump2 cross-jumps their identical stores.
spelling: a local set in each arm and stored in each arm (`area = ALIGN(...); w[1] = area;`, the later reads still from memory: a single store after the join lets cse reuse the value), or one variable carried through (`fields %= 2; dst->field = fields;` in place of a second `field` local).

title: A one-block copy across a call takes the first saved register before global allocation runs.
symptom: registers only: two values that live across a call sit in `s0`/`s1` the other way round (retail keeps the pointer parameter in `s0` and a much-used second parameter in `s1`), and an object built from SDK-exact C allocates like ours while the SDK object allocates like retail.
cause: global-alloc colours by `floor_log2(refs) * refs / live length`, so the parameter with the most uses (a `switch` index) takes `s0` first. A pseudo used in one block is coloured earlier, by local-alloc, which gives a call-crossing one `s0`; the global pseudos live in that block then conflict with `s0`, and the parameter copied into it from `a0` gets `s0` by copy preference. A local copied from the parameter inside one arm stays a pseudo of its own only when cse cannot fold it into the parameter: a set of the same local in the other arm (dead later, and deleted) makes it the longer-lived register of the pair.
spelling: `if (obj != 0) { ply = obj; ... use ply ... } else { ply = 0; ... }` in place of `ply = obj; if (ply != 0) ...`. Read the allocation order from `-dg` (`;; N regs to allocate:`) and the priorities from `-dl` (`Register N used R times across L insns`).

title: A deleted jump to the next block stops fall-through filling for the whole function.
symptom: most conditional branches keep a `nop` where another spelling fills the slot from the following instruction (`beq v0,a0,L; nop; li v1,2` where siblings have `beq v0,a0,L; li v1,2`). Copies from a branch target still fill slots, and the copied original stays in place as dead code (`bnez s4,L+4; slti at,…` with the same `slti` still at `L`). Every slot in the function changes together, whether the cause comes before or after it in the source. Small test files reproduce it.
cause: when the code generator deletes an unconditional jump whose target is the next block, the scheduler stops filling slots from the fall-through for the whole function. The front end has already removed its own redundant jumps, so only jumps made later count. Three constructs produce one: a `return;` closing the last `if` block of a function that returns `void`, or `igResult`, which comes back through a hidden pointer (`if (bad) { report(); return; }` as the final statement); a conditional expression whose condition ends in a logical not as the last operand of `&&` or `||` (`f(x == -1 && !p ? a : b)`; the same condition in an `if` does not count, and neither does `p == 0`); a `switch` with `default:` written before its cases.
unit_text: `src/engine/core/CoreLibrary.cpp`: the arena pool's block walks (0x311d10, a trailing `return;` after the bad-chunk report) and the arena block check (0x312790, `igResult`).
notes: Reading it: when retail has the `nop` slots, look for which of these the function used. One that also changes the branch it sits in (`!p` turns `beqz p,T; b F` into `bnez p,F`) is the wrong one. An `int` or pointer return has no `return;` form; there the trigger has to be one of the other two.

title: A copy the allocator coalesces away leaves a jump the block pass retargets.
symptom: a function has the unfilled slots of the entry above and none of its three constructs; its instructions match with every obvious spelling and only the slots differ (15 `nop`s in a 324-instruction function).
cause: the block pass has three rules, read from the compiler (0x4c6b80) and reported per block by the block dump: it retargets a conditional branch whose target block begins with an unconditional jump, it deletes a jump to the next block, and it merges a block that ends with a jump or the return into its only predecessor when that predecessor falls into it. Any of them empties the predecessor lists. The first one fires when the last statement of an `if` body is a copy between two variables that the register allocator gives one register: `if (pages != 0) { …; if (self->updateStatistics) { …call… } result = pages; } else { …; result = 0; }`. The copy's block is then only the jump over the `else`, and the `updateStatistics` test branches to it. Assigning `result` straight from the calls gives the same instructions with filled slots.
notes: Evidence for the source: the GameCube build of the same function keeps the two variables apart (`mr r29,r25` in front of the jump over the failure arm), and its allocator calls all write `r25`.

Reading it: when a function is in this mode and no jump-making construct fits, run the block dump on the candidate with a suspect spelling and look for the changed block; in the other builds look for a register copy that the PS2 build does not have.

title: A commutative add takes the plain variable as its first operand.
symptom: The front end orders the operands of `+` so that a leaf comes first. An inline call counts as complex until it is expanded, and a conditional expression is always complex. To get retail's `addu v1,a0,v1` with the payload in `a0`, the payload has to be a variable. When the value is only computed after the guards of a check, that means splitting the `&&` chain into nested `if`s and assigning the variable between them: `if (level > 0 && ml > 0) { size = …; if (((Chunk *)((char *)h + (size + header)))->used && ml > 0) … }` compiles to the same branches as the flat chain.

title: A statement after an `if` that both arms reach is hoisted into the test's slot.
symptom: after a scan loop, `bnez t7,L; li s0,2` with the append in the fall-through, and the loop's first exit to that test keeps a `nop`. With the assignment written ahead of the `if` the `li` stays in front of the branch, the slot takes the fall-through's first instruction, and the loop exit copies the `li` from its target. *Cause (not traced):* written after the `if`, the assignment is the first instruction of the join both paths reach, and it ends up in the test's slot; the test is then the first instruction at the loop exits' target, which leaves them nothing to copy. Written ahead, it stays in the test's own block and the slot takes the fall-through's first instruction. The two placements also number the temporaries differently.
spelling: `if (!space) { piece[used++] = c; i++; } state = 2;`.

title: An `else` that only copies keeps the join's first instruction out of the test's slot.
symptom: `beqz a2,L; nop; ori a3,a3,0x10; L: li v1,1` in retail, where `if (linearOnly) colorMode |= 0x10;` moves the `li` into the slot (`beqz a2,L; li v1,1; ori a3,a3,0x10`), the hoist of the entry above. *Cause (block dump):* written `if (linearOnly) variant = colorMode | 0x10; else variant = colorMode;`, the `else` is a copy the allocator coalesces, and its block stays as the branch's target, empty, ahead of the join. The target has no instruction to give, and the fall-through's `ori` writes a register live across the branch, so the slot keeps its `nop`. The predecessor lists are not emptied, and the other slots are unchanged.
spelling: the table index is its own local, assigned in both arms, as in the sibling path that selects `colorMode | 0x18` or `colorMode | 8`.

title: Check the build before looking for a spelling of `movz` or of a slot fill.
symptom: The same probes compiled with `-O4,p -sdatathreshold 2` under 3.0 (011126, `default`), b38 (`combat`) and b52: `movz` from a ternary whose arms are parameters or constants (`c ? a : b`, `c ? 5 : 7`, `c ? a : 0`, `c ? kOff : kOn` with enum constants) on all three. `int` arms `0` and `1` (`c ? 0 : 1`, `c ? 1 : 0`) give `movz` under 3.0 and `sltu` (with `xori` for `c ? 0 : 1`) under b38 and b52. Arms that load (`p->a`) branch on all three. 3.0 fills slots that b38 and b52 leave empty: an `if`/`else if`/`else` of three calls followed by a store has the `b` to the join filled with a copy of the join's first instruction (`li v1,7`, three predecessors) under 3.0 and a `nop` under b38 and b52; a `while (c--) { if (*p) break; p++; }` loop is two instructions shorter under 3.0, where b38 and b52 leave a `nop` between its load and the `bnez` that tests it and another in a slot. A `for` loop summing `p[i]` keeps an index and an add under 3.0 and walks the pointer under b38 and b52. b38 and b52 gave the same listing for every probe.
notes: Probe: `int t1(int c, int a, int b) { return c ? a : b; }`, `int i1(int c) { return c ? 0 : 1; }`, `void u3(int *p, int c) { if (c > 3) g(1); else if (c > 1) g(2); else g(3); p[2] = 7; }`, `int u4(int *p, int c) { while (c--) { if (*p) break; p++; } return *p; }`.

title: Declaration order, getters and helper argument order decide ids.
symptom: A count declared before a cast list pointer (`int count; List *list = (List *)target; count = list->_count;`) gives the list the lower saved register; the natural order swaps them.
unit_text: `src/game/beNDMWShopCtrl00.cpp`. A value an inline helper returns, and a helper's own locals, are numbered with the inline's values; using the getter (`work = buildData(self)`) and the setter inline together gives retail's order where hand-ordered locals stood before. / `src/game/beDemoManager.cpp`. An inline's arguments are evaluated before its body: `AppendRecordString(self->_messenger, db, record, key)` loads the messenger into a saved register before the call inside it. / `src/game/beNDMWShopCtrl00.cpp`.

title: A parameter reached through a cast moves registers; the real class as the parameter type does not.
symptom: `self` and a flag parameter in exchanged saved registers (`s0`/`s1`), or a member read through a computed address (`lw a0,0(v1)` where retail has `lw a0,16(s1)`).
cause: a cast local (`View *v = (View *)self;`) is a declared local with an id of its own, which changes the colouring order; an inline cast on each access (`((View *)self)->f16`) makes `&member` a value the common-subexpression pass shares with the load.
spelling: declare the parameter with its real class and read the reflected fields through it; cast the loaded handle, not the object (`o = (struct Rc *)self->_parentList;`).
unit_text: `src/engine/scenegraph/SceneGraphLibrary.cpp` (0x195970 and the other scene-graph destroy functions).

title: What a declaration changes at the call.
symptom: A `(...)` or K&R `()` declaration and a prototype give the same call when the arguments are word-sized `int`, pointer or enum values, or constants. They differ in these cases, so each is tested on every caller when a declaration moves to its home: a `float` argument behind `(...)` (C++) or `()` (C) is promoted to `double` by a software conversion (8 to 72 bytes more in each of five units tested); a one- or two-byte parameter with a non-constant argument is narrowed by the caller, with `andi` for an unsigned type and `sll`/`sra` for a signed one, so only the real type reproduces retail; a one- or two-byte return is masked at the callers that compare or widen it (the byte-returning entry); a one- or two-byte global is small data under `-sdatathreshold 2`, reached through `gp`; declared as an array it is reached through `lui`/`addiu` (16 bytes more in one function), while larger globals are reached the same way as scalars or arrays; a call that omits an argument: retail passed whatever was already in the register, and the real call names that variable; a typed prototype can change the order in which a caller loads its arguments even with word-sized parameters: giving one image function of the Gfx library a prototype reordered the argument loads of two matched callers.
unit_text: `src/engine/igViewerRenderer.cpp`, `src/engine/p2viewport.c`, `src/game/ParticleArray.cpp` (floats), `src/game/beActionStarter.cpp` (a byte parameter), `src/game/GameMain.cpp` (a byte global), `src/engine/gfx/GfxLibrary.cpp` (0x157990 and 0x1566c0 calling 0x159320).

title: A `const` reference parameter takes its temporary where retail built it.
symptom: A callee taking `const igVec3f &` called with `igVec3f(0, 0, -1.2f)` builds the temporary in retail's frame slot; a named local declared for the call takes another one. A reference is a pointer in the ABI, so the callee's own bytes do not change.

title: A value read once into a local lets a later local colour in its declared order.
symptom: float registers shifted by one: a square root takes `f10` where retail has `f13`, and the three direction components it scales take `f13`..`f11` where retail has `f12`..`f10`. Declaring the root first gives it `f0` and shifts every other float.
cause: the root needs the lowest id of the group, and declared first it has it, but it interferes with 32 float values, so simplify passes over it and pushes it last ([the tracer](#the-register-allocator-tracer)): it colours first and takes `f0`. In retail the other sphere's radius is a declared local ahead of it, live across the root; pushed first, it brings the root's degree to 31, and the root is pushed in its declared order.
spelling: `otherRadius = other->_radius`, read once for the containment tests and the far point, declared first; the root declared before the direction components.

title: A value read through the same expression in every test is one temporary that colours first.
symptom: every long-lived value of a function one register off: the program's capability word in `t9` where retail has `t0`, and the bits taken from it, the loop counters and the hoisted loads each one up.
cause: `IRO_CommonSubs` shares the repeated read of `p2ProgramFlags[p2CurrentProgram]` in a temporary whose id comes after every declared local, so it colours first and takes the lowest free register. Copied into a declared `flags` local it has the lowest id and colours last.
spelling: each capability is read as `(p2ProgramFlags[p2CurrentProgram] >> n) & 1`, as the file's other functions read them, and the locals that hold the bits are declared in the order they are assigned.

title: A class local is numbered after every declared local, wherever it is declared.
symptom: instructions identical, two saved registers exchanged between a result object and a pointer local (`s2`/`s3`). The result declared `int` and read as `.v` matches; declared as its class it does not, and no declaration position of it or of the other locals changes anything.
cause: a class local is not a register candidate. `IRO_ScalarizeClassDataMembers`, the first phase of the optimizer's loop, replaces its one member with a temporary (`*(result) = ...` becomes `*(@1793) = ...` in the dump), and the temporary takes its allocator id then: after all the function's declared locals, mid-block ones included, and after the parameters of the inlines already expanded (`operator==`'s `this`), but before the optimizer's later temporaries and before the second and later webs of a reused variable. Retail colours the pointer first, so the pointer has the later id. No declared pointer can have one; a later web of a variable the function reuses does. Traced: block-local pointer 42, result 49, result coloured first; pointer as a later web 62, result 48, retail's colours.
spelling: `igResult result = g_resultSuccess;`, and the new pool kept in the function's one pool pointer, which the loops before and after it also use, not in a block-local of its own. With the pointer reused both `int` and `igResult` match, so the `int` only compensated for the block-local.

title: An argument that carries an integer conversion is loaded before the plain ones.
symptom: a call passes two fields of one row as its third and fourth arguments and loads the fourth first, with the row pointer in the third's register (`lw a3,4(a2); lw a2,0(a2)`); the plain spelling loads them in order with the row in `a3`. A `(long long)` cast on the fourth argument gives retail's order although the parameter is 32-bit.
cause: the two spellings differ in the IR by one conversion node on that argument. Any conversion to an integer type does it: an implicit one between `int` and `unsigned`, a byte field widened to an `int` or `unsigned` parameter, `(int)` written on an `int` or on a pointer. A cast to a pointer type does not (it is a node too, but it does not count). Of the four combinations (conversion on the third, the fourth, both, neither) the fourth is loaded first exactly when it carries one, and the row pointer takes the register of the argument loaded last. Where the base pointer is not in an argument register, two arguments that both carry a conversion, or neither, are loaded in order.
spelling: the field and the parameter in their own types, which differ in sign: `unsigned size` in the row, `int size` in the callee, the argument passed plain. An `int` field with an `unsigned` parameter gives the same bytes, here and in the callee's other callers; the row's size is printed as `0x%08x` beside its addresses, so the field is the unsigned one.
notes: The reverse case: retail loads a list handle before the byte flag passed after it (`lw a3,192(s1); lbu t0,168(s1)`), and with the flag parameter declared `unsigned int` the flag is loaded first, because the widening is a conversion; `(List *)(int)file->_list` then repairs the order by giving the list one too. The parameter has the field's type, `unsigned char endianSwap`, so neither argument carries a conversion. In the callees the flag is tested plain, `if (endianSwap)`: `endianSwap != 0` promotes the byte, and the promotion the tests share becomes an `andi` into a register of its own (4 bytes more).

An enum parameter: retail loads the source and destination factors and the `short` stage before the byte constant, the source into a temporary moved into `a1` in the call's delay slot (`lw v0,12(a0)` … `move a1,v0`); with `int` parameters the factors load after the context moves into `a0`, 4 bytes short. The callee takes the factors as the reflected enum (`IG_GFX_BLENDING_FUNCTION`) and the caller casts its `int` fields to it, as the texture attribute does for its wrap and filter modes. `(int)` written on the `int` field gives the plain bytes there, and the enum on the source alone leaves 2 words.

title: An `int` copy of a parameter at the top of a function stands for something else.
symptom: *A reassigned variable.* `m = m->_writeProxy ? proxy() : m` makes a second web of `m`, numbered after every declared local, so it colours before the count declared after it and takes its register (`s3`/`s4` exchanged; traced: list 35, `m` 37, count 39, second web of `m` 42). Copies of the list and flag parameters into `int` locals moved their ids instead. The source has two variables, each declared where it is first set: `meta`, `index`, `writeMeta`, `count`, `i`; of the declaration orders only those with `index` before `writeMeta` before `count` before `i` match. *A cast at a call inside a loop.* `(int)file` on a pointer parameter passed to a callee declared with an `int` is a loop-invariant expression: `IRO_MoveInvariantExpressions` computes it into a temporary before the loop, and when that value is spilled the frame has one more 4-byte slot (192 bytes against 176). The callee takes the pointer type and the parameter is passed plain.

title: A loop index started from a named value is declared last.
symptom: a walk over a list from a start count to an end count has the index and the end count in each other's saved register (`s0`/`s1`); the start count is loaded before the end count, so declaring the index first and assigning it there gives the wrong registers, and only an index declared after the count but assigned before it matched.
cause: the source names the start: `int first = base->_count; int count = fields->_count; for (int i = first; i < count; i++)`. The copy `i = first` is propagated, `first` never reaches the allocator and takes no id, and `i`, declared in the `for`, is numbered after `count` (traced: list 33, count 34, index 35; with `int i = base->_count; int count = ...` index 34, count 35).
spelling: as above, each local declared where it is first set. Four field walks of one class take this shape.

title: A value read through an inline getter is numbered after the declared locals.
symptom: a function loads three fields of one global into saved registers and then makes a call; the registers fit no declaration order in which the locals are declared where they are assigned. A search found an order with the first and third of them declared after locals that are first set much later.
cause: a local initialised from an inline function's return value takes the return temporary's id, which is made after all of the caller's declared locals (traced: the two values leave the declared range 33-47 and become node 71 and a neighbour). Controls: both getters are needed; either one alone, or neither, differs; the second field read plainly or through a getter makes no difference.
spelling: the two values through inline member getters of the object that holds them, the other field read directly, and every local declared at its first assignment, loop indices and block-locals in their blocks. No declaration order is left to choose.

title: A typed view of a `void *` parameter is copied where it is declared.
symptom: `beqz system,end; nop; lbu mode; bnez mode; move s1,a0`: the parameter's copy to a saved register sits in the second branch's delay slot and the first slot is empty. Declared at the top of the function the copy fills the first slot.
cause: the copy is an assignment and is emitted in the block that holds it; the delay-slot filler then moves it over the load into the next branch's slot.
spelling: the view declared as the first statement inside the `if (system)` block, the other locals after it where they are first set. A separate local for the mode byte is not needed.

title: C-style declarations at the top keep their order; parameters need no copies.
symptom: A duplicate search over a record table (`i`, `j`, a found flag, the value) has the value in `s0` and the flag in `s1`, though the value is set first: the four are declared together at the top as `int i, j, found; T *value;` (traced ids 34-37). The value or the flag declared in its block exchanges two registers. Six sibling functions share the order. Copies of the output pointer and the remaining count into locals changed nothing: the parameters are stepped directly. The same class walks its records with a pointer declared before the index (`record++` beside `i++`) where retail keeps a stepped pointer, and indexes `records[i]` where retail multiplies on every pass; the unit builds for size and does not turn one into the other.

title: A pointer an inline getter returns is numbered after the caller's block locals.
symptom: a configure function reads strings from its info record at the top and parses each in a block with a local of its own (a flags word, a level); retail gives the block local the higher saved register, the plain spelling gives it to the string, and the only declaration order that matches has the block locals declared at the top, ahead of the strings.
cause: the string read through an inline getter that returns the pointer is the getter's result, numbered with the inline's values after every local the caller declares, block locals included, so it colours first. The getter's parameter may be `const` or not. An `int` getter with the cast at the call, an `int` local and a plain field read all keep the declared local's early number.
spelling: `const char *messages = igMemoryPoolInfo_messages(info);` with `static inline const char *igMemoryPoolInfo_messages(const igMemoryPoolInfo *info)`, every local declared where it is first set, the result an `igResult` assigned from the base call.
unit_text: `src/engine/core/CoreLibrary.cpp` (0x3223d0, 0x325940, the arena pool's). / `src/game/beMessenger.cpp` (0x38d0a0). In the generator's update the work, the data and the player data go through inline helpers too, and so does the enemy record number inside the setter: the id-order search could not find it because the ids come from where a value is created, with `database` < the model-name temporaries < `recNo` < the reload of `created`, and `ready` < `work` < `data` < `playerData`. The example is `beGenerater_UpdateRam` (0x384c40).
notes: Also found: a row pointer the loop reads (`DelayAt(self, i)` in a frozen-delay loop, which no declaration order could fix: the `a1`/`a2` swap), a send time read through `SendTimeOf(const Delay *)` (a plain read becomes `+=` and flips the `daddu` operands), and a list the loop appends to (`TimeListOf(node)` in a meter update: the list lands in `s0` and every saved register follows).

title: A decoder's helpers take the cursor and the result by reference, and the results are typed scratch locals.
symptom: a record decoder runs a variable-length-integer loop per field. Retail keeps the read pointer in one saved register throughout, the flags word in the next and the slot counter between them; the value and the shift of a field's loop sit in `a1` and `a0`. Helpers that return the advanced pointer, or that build the value in a local of their own and store it at the end, give the same instructions with the saved registers rotated and the value and shift exchanged; no declaration order of the caller's locals changes anything, because each is replaced by a helper's temporary.
cause: a helper that works on `T &out` directly (`out = 0; out |= ...`) leaves the caller's declared variable as the accumulator, with the id of its declaration; the helper's own locals (shift, a copy of the cursor) are numbered after it. Only the first web of a declared variable has that id: a scratch variable used for a second field is a later web and is numbered after the helper's locals, which exchanges the two registers. Retail's pattern (declared-variable order at the type, at the first signed field and at the first unsigned field after it, later-web order everywhere else) is three variables: the type, one signed scratch and one unsigned scratch, each field assigned from the scratch of its own signedness.
spelling: `static inline void decodeUnsigned(const char *&p, unsigned int &out)` and `decodeSigned(const char *&p, int &out)`, called as `decodeSigned(p, value); record->size = value;`.
notes: The cursor copy: each helper reads through a local copy (`const char *q = p; ... p = q;`). The copy's last assignment back is then an expression the optimizer puts into the next use in the same block, so where two fields are decoded with a call between them and no branch, the cursor's increment comes after the call's result is stored (`jal; lw a0,68(s4); sw v0,68(s3); addiu s0,s0,1`), not in the call's delay slot.

title: A character compared in place needs no local.
symptom: A scan `while (*s && *s != '\'' && n < 255)` whose body tests and stores `*s` again shares one load and one sign extension; copying the character to an `int` local in the condition (`(c = *s) != '\''`) gives the same instructions with eight temporaries permuted.

title: Stack slots rise as allocator ids fall, and a split lifetime has a late id.
symptom: instructions and registers match and two or three spilled values sit in each other's 16-byte slots (`sw zero,208(sp)` against `sw zero,256(sp)`), or the entry block zeroes two slots in the other order.
cause: the slots are handed out upwards from the highest id to the lowest. Ids are: declared locals in declaration order, then the optimizer's temporaries in the order it makes them (a shared mask or a shared `unsigned short` to `int` conversion among them), then the temporaries of `IRO_SplitLifetimes`. That phase gives a variable with several separate lifetimes (zeroed at entry and set again on the reallocation path, and set and used on its own on the free path) a new temporary for every lifetime but the second it finds in statement order; so the lifetime that starts at the entry assignment has a late id, and the one on the free path keeps the declared one. It handles the variables in the order the function first refers to them, a dead initialiser included, and makes one variable's temporaries together. The scheduler trace prints the ids (`D:c0r90 U:c0r0` is `r90 = 0`), and the optimizer dump after `IRO_SplitLifetimes` shows the temporaries by name.
spelling: declarations in the order the slots of the unsplit variables fall (`int newBytes; int total; bool moved; int oldHeadBytes;` for slots 256, 240, 224, 208), and the entry assignments as statements in the order of the stores. One function needs `int oldHeadBytes = 0;` ahead of `oldSize = 0; oldBytes = 0; oldHeadBytes = 0;`: the dead initialiser only makes it the first of the three the phase handles. What the original's earlier reference was is not known. The GameCube build zeroes exactly the split variables with register copies (`li r26,0; mr r19,r26; mr r24,r26`) and the others with `li`, which shows which variables the original reused across the free and reallocation paths.
notes: Open: the malloc pool's sibling (0x3236a0) shows the same three copies on GameCube, yet matches on PS2 only with the free path's sentinel offset in a local of its own: with the variable reused there its entry lifetime takes a late id and its slot falls below the shared alignment's. One source for both functions has not been found.

title: Spilled locals take their stack slots from the last declared to the first.
symptom: A function with more long-lived locals than saved registers keeps some in 16-byte frame slots; the slots rise in the reverse of declaration order, so their offsets give the declaration block. Where a value returned after a scoped block has a slot below the block's own locals, the locals are all declared at the top of the function, C style, and only the scoped object is in the block. The hidden result pointer of a function that returns a class is kept differently when registers run out: it goes to a 4-byte slot beside the address-taken locals (`sw a0,360(sp)` at entry, loaded at each `return`), not to a 16-byte slot.

title: Fields read where they are used leave no locals to order.
symptom: A reader's `gets` compares, clamps and subtracts its position and length: `if (f->pos >= f->len) return 0;` and `if (n + f->pos >= f->len) n = f->len - f->pos;`. The shared reads are the optimizer's temporaries, numbered as it makes them; `int len = f->len; int pos = f->pos;` loads the same two words into exchanged registers, and matched only with the locals declared in the reverse of the order they are set.
unit_text: `src/engine/core/CoreLibrary.cpp` (0x2ecea0, 0x32bdd0). A stack pool's free space is `(unsigned)(pool->end + 1) - pool->top` straight from the fields, and the running `end` and `low` are declared in the branch that walks them; the padding step reads `pool->top` in place (`mask & (align - (pool->top & mask))`, `out[i] = pool->top + pad`). Locals for the top, declared at the head of the function, exchanged registers and changed the order of the size arithmetic. **A reused index is numbered late.** One `unsigned i` serving every loop of a function has a web per loop, and each web after the first is numbered after all the declared locals, so the index takes a lower register than the locals of the loop it runs. An index per loop takes the higher one. Seventeen locals whose order a search had found reduce to the function written this way, with the count an `unsigned short` parameter used directly (its widened copy is the compiler's and takes the lowest register, where a declared count local took a higher one). / `src/engine/core/CoreLibrary.cpp` (0x327d40, 0x327ed0). A scanf over a format string reads `format[i]` at each use in the outer dispatch (`if (format[i] != '%')`, `piece[used++] = format[i]`), and only the inner conversion scan keeps the character in a local, `c`, with the space test through a one-line inline (`static inline int isSpace(int c) { return _ctype_[c + 1] & 8; }`). A character local for the outer dispatch, declared anywhere, exchanged it with the hoisted copy of the format pointer (`t1`/`t2`); without the inline, ten temporaries took other registers. / `src/engine/core/CoreLibrary.cpp` (0x2ec980, 0x32b8d0).

title: Where a pair of locals is all that is left of an order.
symptom: `for (int i = 0, count = list->count; i < count; i++)` numbers the index before the count, which a count declared in front of the loop does not; an `int` getter for the count changes nothing.
unit_text: `src/engine/core/CoreLibrary.cpp` (0x2e8c40). Two values that never cross a call share the argument registers, and the later-numbered takes `a0`: a heap walk's next-block pointer is declared with the function's other pointers, ahead of its `ok` flag, and every other local sits where it is first set. / `src/engine/core/CoreLibrary.cpp` (0x312790). An index declared at the head of the function (`int i; int seen = 0; bool found = false;`) is numbered before the counters zeroed beside it and takes the higher temporary register. / `src/engine/core/CoreLibrary.cpp` (0x306510).

title: The front end orders the operands of a commutative operator.
symptom: `addu v1,v1,a0` where retail has `addu v1,a0,v1`, and exchanging the operands in the source changes nothing.
cause: MWCC rewrites `a + b` before the optimizer runs; the first phase of the IR dump already shows the new order. A plain variable goes ahead of an expression, and the shorter of two expressions first. A call of an inline function is an expression at that point, even one that expands to a single temporary, so `size(p) + (p->words + 1) * 4` becomes `(p->words + 1) * 4 + @temp`.
spelling: give the term retail adds first a local of its own (`payload = size(p); total = payload + ...`), or put the whole sum in the inline, where the left term is the inline's own local.

title: An inline's return value replaces the variable it is assigned to.
symptom: two saved registers exchanged, and no declaration order of the locals moves them.
cause: in `total = sum(p)` copy propagation replaces `total` with the inline's return temporary, which takes its allocator id after every declared local. A local assigned an expression that only contains the inline's result (`total = payload + ...`) keeps the id of its declaration.
spelling: as above; the destination then colours by where it is declared.

title: A value read through an accessor inline is numbered with the inline's values.
symptom: A saved flag (`used = usedBit(p)`), a link store whose value is loaded (`setForward(p, *bin)`) and a size kept in a named local rather than updated in place each gave retail's temporaries where the written-out expression exchanged two of them.

title: m2c offset variables steal saved registers.
symptom: A user `offset += 4` with `data + offset` is a source variable coloured before the slot pointer; an index loop over `&data[i]` lets the compiler make the offset itself, with retail's registers. Rewrite m2c's strength-reduced loops as index loops first.

title: A derived view of a base-class parameter keeps the argument register.
symptom: A traversal function that takes `igTraversal *traversal`, works through `igCompileTraversal *self = (igCompileTraversal *)traversal;` and passes `traversal` on to the next traversal function keeps the incoming `a0` live for that call: the code between avoids `a0` and the call has no `move a0,s0`. One pointer used for both gives the move and shifts every temporary.

title: Inline virtuals are emitted in reverse declaration order.
symptom: Declare them in the reverse of retail's address order.

title: A later web of a reused variable colours first; a block local is its own first web.
symptom: instructions identical, the temporaries of one path rotated (`v1`/`a0`, then every temporary after them), and no order of the declarations changes it.
cause: `IRO_SplitLifetimes` gives each separate lifetime of a variable after the first a new temporary, numbered late, so it colours before the optimizer's shared values and takes the low register. The value retail colours late is a variable's first lifetime. In the dlmalloc code one `bck` holds the chunk before the victim in the small-bin path, in the unsorted loop, in binning and in the bin scan; retail's colours need the first two to be lifetimes of their own.
spelling: the value declared in the block that uses it (`TaggedBlockHeader *previous = ...;` in the small-bin path and again in the unsorted loop), the function-level variable left to the paths that share it. The reverse case in the same allocator: the end and the new top of a separately placed system block are the function's `newEnd` and `newTop` assigned a second time, which is what gives them the first temporary registers; a local for the end exchanges three temporaries, and the sum written out at both uses is computed after the alignment test instead of before it.

title: A named local keeps an argument out of the inline's arithmetic.
symptom: `addiu a2,s5,-8; addiu a0,a2,-4; ... addiu v0,a2,-12`: the argument is computed once and the inline subtracts from it. Passed as an expression (`resize(chunk, size - 8)`) the constants fold (`-12`, `-20` from the variable); a `const` parameter changes nothing, a cast on the argument stops the folding but numbers the value differently.
spelling: `unsigned int shortened = size - 8; resize(chunk, shortened);`.

title: Locals declared in the order they are first assigned.
symptom: A search over the declaration order of fourteen locals found one that matched; testing every single move showed only five constraints, and the order of first assignment satisfies them all. Try that order before searching.

title: A 64-bit member passed as `%u` is read through a getter.
symptom: a notice passes twelve 64-bit counters truncated to 32 bits. Retail loads the first five whole (`ld`) before the branch of a conditional argument and truncates them after it (`dsll32`/`dsra32`), loads the seven that go to the stack with `lw`, all of them ahead of the stores; the candidate loads and stores one by one and reads the first five with `lw` after the conditional.
cause: a cast on the member is narrowed to a 32-bit load in the optimizer and is then a plain operand, loaded where its argument register is set. An inline getter returning `long long` leaves a 64-bit temporary assigned where the call stands, so every argument is evaluated before any is placed, and the truncation happens at placement; within one block the load and the truncation merge into `lw`.
spelling: `(unsigned int)pool->getLocalAllocated()` with `long long getLocalAllocated()`.

title: An `int` accessor materialises a flag test.
symptom: `andi v0,v0,0x40; sltu v0,zero,v0; beqz v0`: the option test goes through an inline returning `int` (`return (flags & option) != 0;`). Written in place, or through an inline returning `bool`, the `sltu` is folded into the branch.

title: A copy that coalescing removes leaves its block behind.
symptom: `beqz at,L730` to a block that is only `b L1138`: the source assigns `newp = oldp` at the end of the first arm, both variables take one register, and the jump is not threaded because the block was not empty when jumps were chained. The statements after the arms use `newp`. An assertion written ahead of `remainder_size = newsize - nb` likewise leaves the subtraction on both sides of the notice.

title: A read through a `const` getter and a store to the member do not share the member's address.
symptom: a local record's member is read, then stored to inside a loop, each time straight off the stack (`lw v0,244(sp)` … `sw v0,244(sp)`); plain reads and stores put the member's address in a saved register for the whole block (`addiu s5,sp,292; lw v0,0(s5)` … `sw v0,0(s5)`) and the frame grows by the slots that displaces. In the same function a member read three times around calls does keep its address in a register (`addiu s5,sp,244; lw a0,0(s5)`).
cause: the address `&local + offset` is an expression `IRO_CommonSubs` shares when it is used twice on one path. A read through a `const` member function has its address node marked, the plain store's is not, so those two are different expressions; three plain reads are one.
spelling: `if (event.getSourceFile() == 0 || …) { int *frame = event.getCallStack(); … event.callStack = frame; event.f68 = path; }` with `const` getters on the record, and the later fields read plainly.

title: A by-value getter in a variadic call is read before a conditional argument.
symptom: `lb v0,976(sp); beqz v0,L; lw a2,184(sp)`: the value passed after `spec[0] != 0 ? spec : "0x%08x"` is loaded ahead of the conditional's branch. An inline getter's result is a temporary assigned where the call stands, before the conditional is evaluated; the member written in place is loaded where its argument register is set, after it. Pointer members tested first (`if (event.group != 0 && …)`) are already in a register and need no getter.

title: A pointer cast to `int` at several calls is one value in a saved register.
symptom: With the record's accessors declared `(int record, int slot)`, `(int)&event` at each call was shared as an expression and kept in `s5` from the top of the function, and every other saved register moved; declared with the record pointer, each call builds `addiu a0,sp,176` in place.

title: A `switch` with one case keeps the branch pair.
symptom: `beq v1,v0,body; nop; b past` for a block run for a single event type is `switch (event.type) { case 8: …; break; }`; `if (event.type == 8)` gives `bne v1,v0,past`. A `case 15:` written in front of `default:` shows in the jump table's bound (`sltiu at,v0,16`, not 15).

title: An element read through a reference accessor keeps `base + offset` when the index is hoisted.
symptom: `lw v1,16(v0); lw v0,176(sp); addu v0,v1,v0; lh v0,0(v0)`: the list's data plus a byte offset computed once in front of the loop. With `list->_data[index]` (or a by-value `get(index)`) the same two values are added the other way round, `addu v0,v0,v1`.
cause: `IRO_MoveInvariantsInAddressExpr` rewrites the address under an indirection inside a loop with the invariant part first, `(index << 1) + data`, before `IRO_MoveInvariantExpressions` moves the shift out. An accessor that returns a reference leaves the address in its return temporary through the first round of loop phases, so it is not under an indirection when that rewrite runs: only the shift is moved, the order stays as written, and the temporary is put back into the read in the next round.
spelling: `T &operator[](int index) { return _data[index]; }` on the list, `(*bases.p)[parentIndex]`.

title: Statement order decides which temporaries share a register with a reloaded spill.
symptom: `lw v0,208(sp); addiu s6,s6,1; lw v1,8(s4); addu s5,s5,v0; lhu v0,20(s4); addu v0,v1,v0`: the reloaded step and the size share `v0`, so the cursor's step was written ahead of the statement that reads the size (`slot++; field += step; meta->_sizeofSize = offset(field) + size(field);`). With the size update first, the reload overlaps both loads and takes a third register. The two members go through by-value getters: read in place, the widened `unsigned short` is evaluated ahead of the `int` on its left.

title: A `short` updated in place is sign-extended where it is computed.
symptom: `addu v0,s6,v0; dsll32 s6,v0,16; dsra32 s6,s6,16` ahead of a list append is `slot += bases[owner]; list->append(slot);` on a `short` local; the sum passed as the argument is truncated only by the store. The append is the list's own (`n = count(); if (n < _capacity) _count = _count + 1; else List_Resize(this, n + 1, sizeof(T));`): its count comes through the `const` accessor, so the increment reads the member again.

title: A local declared ahead of a spilled one colours after the scan that follows the spill.
symptom: a write position and the byte total it follows share `s5` where retail has `s0`, with the block pointer and the guard size one register low; no order of the function-level locals moves them.
cause: the allocator pushes low-degree nodes in ascending id, scan after scan, and colours in reverse. The last scan pushed the header pointers and the position first and the long-lived locals after them (`45 46 81 | 33 36 37 38`), so the position coloured after them. A position declared before the spilled `first` record pointer has a lower id than the header pointers, is pushed in the same scan as the long-lived locals and after them, colours first and takes `s0`; the byte total, which does not overlap it, then takes `s0` too.
spelling: in the block, `char *cursor; GangRecord *first; TaggedBlockHeader *h;`; at the top the guard before the block pointer.

title: A node one neighbour over the limit waits a scan and takes `v0`.
symptom: a size loop's index is in `v0` and every temporary one register up (`v1`, `a0`, …) where retail has the index in `a3`. The sibling function with one fewer spilled value matches with the same source.
cause: the index has 29 neighbours (traced with the proxy compiler); 25 or more keeps a node out of the scan until enough lower-numbered neighbours are pushed, and only four were (the loop's size, chunk and the inline's two values). Pushed in the second scan, it coloured before all the loop's temporaries. A fifth lower-numbered neighbour puts it in the first scan.
spelling: the member's size with its record is a variable set twice, `entry = chunk + 12; entry = roundUp8(entry); total += entry;`. A variable set once is propagated away and gives no node.

title: Mixed signedness keeps two additions, and two masks, apart.
symptom: `roundUp8(chunk + 12)` with an `int` parameter adds 12 and then 7 where two `unsigned` values fold to 19; a chunk size computed in `int` loads its own `-4` where an `unsigned` one reuses the mask already in a register. Each is a conversion node between the two operations.

title: A header written by the shared inline keeps the arithmetic its other callers need.
symptom: a function that always writes the 12-byte header computes the header word count at run time (`addiu a2,a1,12; subu a1,a2,a1; srl; addiu -1`), and with the statements written out the constant folds; with the fold prevented by a signed local the instructions are retail's but 79 sit elsewhere in the block, the `0 & 1` of the cleared flags in `t9` instead of `v0`.
cause: the pool's blocks are stamped by one inline that takes the block's byte count or 0 (`if (total == 0) total = ((size + 3) & ~3) + 12;` in the long branch, `+ 4` in the short one, then `words = ((total - ((size + 3) & ~3)) >> 2) - 1`) and a flag that forces the long form. The forced branch is removed after the subtraction has been built from two copies of the rounded size, so nothing folds, and the statements reach the scheduler in the inline's order.
spelling: `initBlockHeader(self, h, size, 0, marked, external)`; the two gang allocators and the system-block allocator share it.

title: A compare written toward the larger side branches through `at`.
symptom: `total + used <= max` gives retail's `sltu at,max,sum; bnez at` and puts the refused path out of line; `max >= sum` makes a register of the compare. `alignment > 8` likewise for `slti at,v0,9`.

title: A member call loads its argument before its object.
symptom: `lw a1,124(sp); jal; lw a0,64(s0)` where the candidate has `lw a0,64(s0); jal; lw a1,124(sp)`: the same two loads, the object's issued first. Casts, `get()` and an inline member wrapper change nothing. *Cause (not traced):* MWCC writes a member function's arguments before its `this`; the plain call wrote the object pointer first here. An inline wrapper is expanded and its call is plain again.
spelling: declare the out-of-line member on the class view (`int addDirectory(igObject *directory);`) and map its mangled name to the retail address in the unit's `externals`.

title: A virtual call's object read in its own statement is loaded ahead of a conditional argument.
symptom: Retail loads the object into `a1` in the slot of the branch that picks the text argument (`bnez a3,L; lw a1,148(sp)`); written in the call, the object is loaded at the join after the conditional expression. A local (`igInfoView *loader = (igInfoView *)poolInfo.p;`) before the call gives retail's order.

title: Discarded `igResult` temporaries take frame slots in the order they are made.
symptom: The first made has the highest slot. Calls written in an inline helper make their temporaries when the helper is expanded, after the caller's own, so two allocator loops moved into a helper gave their results the two lowest slots where retail has them above the one the function body makes later. Written in place, the loops give retail's slots. A named result local (`int copied; f(&copied, ...)`) takes a slot ahead of every temporary; the call returning `igResult` makes a temporary where it is.

title: An inline's parameter is numbered before its locals.
symptom: A string setter inline that takes the object as a parameter gives the interned token the first saved register and the object the second; retail has them the other way in one of two call sites. The tracer asks for the object's id after the token's; taking the holder by reference and reading the object into a local declared after the token gives it. In the movie controller's message handler the setter's local takes the interned token directly from the call and is declared before the object pointer, and the setter reads the pointer from a smart pointer it takes by reference: the four values then get ids token 1 < object 1 < token 2 < object 2, all four are pushed in that order in the last scan, and object 2 is coloured first (`s1`), token 2 second (`s2`). Each of these alone leaves 13 words: the object pointer declared first, a setter taking the raw pointer, the token returned through an inline instead of the setter's local.

title: A list append's count must be numbered before its list.
symptom: igSorter's endCompoundRenderPackage appends one package to one of three lists; with the kit's `igTDataList<T>::append(const T &)` (or any helper taking the list) every instruction matches but the sorter sits in `s2` and the lists in `s1`, where retail has them the other way. In the allocator's graph each list has degree 25 (K) and stays until the second scan, where the sorter, the lowest id, is pushed first and so coloured after the lists. The list is the inline's parameter and numbered before the inline's `count` local, and `int n = list->count()` is an `int` copy of an inline's result, numbered late as well. Relabelling the dumped graph (`regalloc_sim.py`) gives retail's colours as soon as each count's id is below its list's: the count (degree 24) is pushed in the first scan, its list drops to 24 and follows in that same scan, and the sorter is pushed after both. Spelling: each append written out in its branch with `int count;` declared ahead of the list pointer, the count read through the flat list's `const int &getCount()` (a plain read that keeps the declaration's id) and `_count++`, which then reloads the count as retail does (`count = _count` folds the reload into the count). A list local declared before the count, a function-level count and list shared by the three branches (one web each), and a helper copying its list parameter into a local declared after the count (coalesced) each leave the 35 words.

title: How a call's arguments are lowered (probed under `#pragma schedule off`).
symptom: Three steps, in this order: An argument that contains a call, an inline with a statement body included, is evaluated first: `f3(p->x, q->y, g())` calls `g` before it loads either field. Every other argument is made ready. One that carries a conversion is loaded here, ahead of the constants: `fi(5, 6, p->s)` with an `int` parameter and `fs3(5, 6, (short)p->x)` with a `short` one start with `lh a2`. A plain load only has its base kept (`move v0,a1` when the base's register is about to be filled), and a computed value is computed (`addiu a1,a2,1`). The argument registers are then filled in parameter order, constants and deferred loads together: `f3(p->x, k + 1, q->y)` gives `addiu a1,a2,1; lw a0,0(a0); lw a2,4(v0)`, `fs3(5, 6, p->s)` gives `li a0,5; li a1,6; lh a2,8(v0)`. A ninth argument is stored to the stack before `a0` to `t3` are filled. A constant both stored and passed is built once into a temporary and copied: `p->x = 10; f3(10, p->y, 3);` gives `li v0,10; sw v0,0(a0); move a0,v0`, not `li a0,10`. "An argument that carries an integer conversion is loaded before the plain ones" (above) is the second step.
notes: Probe: `struct S { int x; int y; short s; };` with the calls quoted, `void fs3(int, int, short);`, `void fi(int, int, int);`, and `static inline int inl(S *p) { int t = p->y; if (t) t++; return t; }` passed as `f3(p->x, inl(q), 7)`.

title: Values the code generator hoists take code-selection ids, after the compare temporaries.
symptom: in a changed-bit scan retail holds the previous word in `a0` and the current compare temporary in `a1`; every spelling has them the other way round (ten words), however its loop, declarations and compares are written.
cause: a value the optimizer hoists is one of its variables and has an id before the compare temporaries. A value the code generator hoists (the data loads, the address adds, the words) takes its id in code selection, after them. Retail's registers need the second kind.
spelling: the mask words read through the holder, `(*(MaskListRef &)current)[material]` with `MaskListRef` an `igSmartPointer<igTDataList<int> >`, using the holder's `operator T *() const` and the list's reference `operator[]` (the idiom of the sound controller): the optimizer then hoists only the two pointer reads, and the reference `operator[]` keeps the address as data first, then offset. A plain read differs by 14 lines, a by-value `get()` by 4. The scan is a plain `for` with `break`. The `li a3,1` shared by `1 << bit` and `_wkChgFlag = 1` comes from the code generator and needs no source.

title: `!=` between two inline calls expands its right operand first.
symptom: `HasPlayer(current[m], bit) != HasPlayer(previous[m], bit)` makes the right call's temporaries first. The two results as `bool` locals declared in order, `bool now = …; bool was = …; if (now != was)`, give retail's order; without them 4 lines differ.

title: An inlined callee's holders are laid out below the caller's own.
symptom: two `igSmartPointer<igObject>` holders at frame offsets 140 and 136 and a string reference below them, where retail has the holders at 136 and 132 and the string reference at 140; the exception table's actions (slot 136, slot 132 with the holder destructor, slot 140 with the string reference's) then differ.
spelling: the data-list setup as `static inline ensureDataList(ram)`: its holders are laid out below the caller's own string reference. The same helper replaces the hand-written setup blocks of the unit's other message handler and still matches.

title: A value that stays live across a loop is numbered late when it is read through a getter.
symptom: two saved registers exchanged (`s0`/`s1`) between an object's ram pointer and a vertex array, in a function with three loops.
cause: the vertex array as a declared local has an id right after the parameters. In the scan before the last one its degree is 26 (19 physical registers, the ram, six values of the third loop) and it only falls below the limit in the final rescan, where the ram (id 32) goes first and is coloured second, so it gets `s1`. With at least two loop locals numbered below the array it is pushed a scan earlier, the ram is pushed last and coloured first (`s0`). Declaring `stride`, `i` and `k` at the top proves it, and only in that order: the order of `i` and `k` decides `a2`/`a1`, and `stride` after `i` moves `a3`.
spelling: the array read through an inline getter, `VertexArray(ram)`, so the value takes the getter's return id after every declared local; every other local is declared where it is first set (`int stride = …`, `for (int i …)`, `for (int k …)`) and the virtual calls cast at the call. The code written out, the getter with a view cast on the initialiser and the getter copied into a view local leave 24 words. `int digit;` is declared before the loop index, at the head of the branch (inside the loop 8 words differ); that line carries a `matching construct` note.

title: A physical `a0` that is live across a block in retail and not in the source: the runtime-call register mask leaks from an earlier file.
symptom: in a meter update's hp block every temporary is one register higher in retail (`a1`-`a3` where the source has `a0`-`a2`, 15 words); in a generator update's fill switch retail has `lw a1,52(s3); li v1,116; lb a1,0(a1); beq a1,v1` where the source has `a0` (3 words; the switches of cases 0 and 2 use `a0` in both builds).
cause: the helper that emits a runtime call (`0x4ba430`) takes the call's used registers from one global mask (general registers at `0x567280`, float bits at `0x567284`); the code that loads a runtime call's arguments (`0x4ba450`, `0x4ba580`) adds each argument register to it with `or`, and nothing in the executable writes it back to zero. Every runtime call compiled later in the same compiler process therefore also uses those registers, later files included. The `__fixsfdi` call in the meter's hp block uses only `f12` in a fresh process; after an earlier `(float)longlong` (`__floatdisf`, argument in `a0`) it uses `a0` too, so physical `a0` is live from the function's entry up to that call, which is the interference that reproduces retail's colours (replaying the allocator with `a0` made to interfere reproduces every one). In the generator the `__fixsfdi` on case 1's path reads `a0` with no write between `beGenerater_SpawnEnemies` and the call.
spelling: none inside the unit; the unit's row in `config/SLUS-20836/units.tsv` names the session prelude `config/SLUS-20836/session-preludes/runtime_call_a0.cpp`, which compiles a `(float)longlong` conversion first in the same compiler process ([build system](../build-system.md#session-preludes)). An unused `static` function with that conversion in the file before the affected function also sets the bit, but retail does not emit it.
unit_text: `beMeterCtrl_UpdateRam` (`0x38fa50`, `src/game/beMeterCtrl.cpp`) and `beGenerater_UpdateRam` (`0x384c40`, `src/game/beGenerater.cpp`) are matched through the session prelude. Without it neither matches.
notes: Evidence: compiling a one-line prelude, `extern "C" float LeakA0(long long x) { return (float)x; }`, ahead of the unit in the same compiler process makes both whole units match; a `(double)int` (`litodp`) prelude does as well, while `long long` division (`a0` and `a1`) and `(double)float` (`f12` only) do not. Retail's meter and generater units contain no runtime call with an integer argument; in link order `beLOA_Traverse` (`0x389bc0`, `__floatdisf`) and `LuaAPI_Dispatch` (`0x370780`, `litodp`) do. That the original build compiled several files in one compiler session is an inference; the leak does not reach every file (`beAction2_OnMessageText` puts a temporary in `a0` before its `__fixsfdi`), so which files carry it depends on the original build order, which is not known.

No spelling: no source text inside the unit produces the `a0` use. Meter: `int` locals for the hp values, an hp pointer local, a percent local, the percent as an inline helper (with and without an unused `self`), a shared `nonZero` flag, a variadic conversion call, the implicit conversion; `igTDataList::append` and `static` are worse (88 and 32 lines). Generator: the selector as an `if`, as `unsigned`, through an index, a local, an inline or a variable shared by the three switches; `default:` before or after the case; the timer start as `return`, `break`, an inline or with a time local; case 1 as one inline; `total` placed elsewhere; an explicit or variadic `__fixsfdi`; a variadic `StartTimer`; double constants. All 23 conversion and call spellings tried leave the call using `f12` only. A standalone test of the same shape also gives `a0`, and no matched function in the census has the pattern.

title: Stack slots: address-taken named locals take the top slots, by-value temporaries the slots below.
symptom: spill and local slots of a function that builds vectors from calls sit in another order than retail's.
notes: Rule: named locals whose address is taken take the top slots in source declaration order, whatever their scope; the temporaries of by-value results come below them in the order they were created. Declaring a vector where it is initialised, rather than at the top, moves its slot.

title: An argument that contains a call is evaluated with the calls, in order, before plain loads.
symptom: Inlines count: a work's sub-command pointer read through an inline accessor is loaded right after the rotation, as in retail, where the same field passed plainly is loaded only at the call. Arguments that contain calls are evaluated left to right, so the parameter order of a call whose float arguments travel in registers can be read from the order of the calls in front of it.

title: An `asm` statement without outputs is volatile already.
symptom: Its keyword does not keep it or move it; strip it. A review of the Sony kernel rows found 47 of their 63 keywords removable. The keyword still changes the code around it when the block has a peephole candidate (next entry), so run the strip test on the whole function.

title: A `volatile` `asm` statement opens a basic block that the peephole skips (probed).
symptom: The code generator starts a block at an `__asm__ volatile(...)` statement, with or without outputs, and marks it (block flag `0x80` in `gdb_pcode.py`'s dump, `0x04` otherwise). The PCode peephole then leaves the rest of that block alone: `bool b = !!(s & 1);` after the statement keeps `sltu; xori 1; xori 1; andi 0xff`, as `#pragma peephole off` does, while a plain `__asm__` (with or without outputs), an MWCC `asm { }` block, an `asm` function earlier in the file or a `volatile` statement in an earlier block or function leaves the peephole on and folds the pair to `sltu`. The GameCube 1.2.5 rule that an `asm` function turns the peephole off for the rest of the file does not hold on b52.
notes: Probe: `int f(int *p, int s) { __asm__ volatile("sync"); bool b = !!(s & 1); if (*p == -1) return g; if (b) return SignalSema(*p); return iSignalSema(*p); }`, then without `volatile`, with `asm { mfc0 s, $12 }`, and with `if (q) g = 2;` between the statement and `b`.

title: Sony's input-operand form.
symptom: A `$gp` store spelled with its word as an output (`"=m"`) can be moved and needs the keyword; Sony's text passes it as an input, `__asm__("sw $28,%0" : : "m"(word))`, which is fixed already. A `"memory"` clobber, as every helper in Sony's `eekernel.h` has, does what a keyword on a syscall statement did.

title: MWCC's `__I_<mnemonic>` builtins are inline assembly.
symptom: They emit one named instruction from C (`__I_mfc0(3, 12)`), and count as `asm` uses.

title: A `static` C function holding one `asm` block gives the same bytes and caller effect as an `asm` function.
symptom: The caller's argument registers stay live across a call to any `static` function defined earlier that contains inline assembly; that proves "static, earlier, contains asm", not "asm function".

title: Hand-written assembly shows in alignment and MMI.
symptom: A 4-aligned object or a loop top at 4 mod 8 under ee-gcc 2.96, `lui`/`ori` for -1 where 2.96 uses `addiu`, and MMI byte operations (`psubb`, `pcpyh`, `psubw`) with no C spelling: the R5900 string and memory routines.

title: MWCC's assembler writes `li reg,0` as `addi`.
symptom: In an MWCC `asm` function `li a1,0` assembles to `addi a1,zero,0`; retail's constant builds have `ori a1,zero,0`, which the source writes out.

title: Three shapes only `volatile` gives under ee-gcc 2.96.
symptom: No type, alias set, pointer spelling or statement barrier has reproduced these, so a function that needs one of them was compiled with a `volatile` access (the owner still decides the row, [source approvals](source-approvals.md)): a load or store kept out of a delay slot: a plain access before a `jal`, or at the head of a branch's target, is always taken into the slot (`bnel; lw` where retail has `bne; nop` and the load after it), and `do { } while (0)` does not stop it; the single-use `lui`, `addiu`, `0(reg)` address form with no call or block boundary before it; a store followed by a load of the same address, or two reads with nothing between them: no spelling makes the compiler forget a value at the same address. The alias-set causes (enum, pointer types, address-taken locals, `-fno-strict-aliasing`) only order accesses to different addresses and reach none of the three.
unit_text: `src/cri/mwsfsvr.c` (0x29ad40, the slot), `src/cri/svm.c` (0x27ec50, `sw; lw` back to back: 88 bytes against 84 without the keyword).
